LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: PARAGRAPH WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing, part of Writing in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is greeting important? 2. How does a lack of sequence affect the meaning of texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. organise ideas coherently for effective communication

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose a well- sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop an interest in writing Arabic.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. organise ideas coherently for effective communication

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose a well- sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly,

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop an interest in writing Arabic.

   Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to construct simple sentences on formal greetings to express their feelings,

2. reorganise jumbled-up sentences to form a meaningful paragraph,

3. use a digital device to play a digital language game involving dragging and dropping sentences to form complete and coherent paragraphs,

4. compose a well-sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to construct simple sentences on formal greetings to express their feelings,
2. reorganise jumbled-up sentences to form a meaningful paragraph,
3. use a digital device to play a digital language game involving dragging and dropping sentences to form complete and coherent paragraphs,
4. compose a well-sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when composing a well- sequenced paragraph neatly and legibly.

• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology when playing a digital language game involving

dragging and dropping sentences to form complete and coherent paragraphs.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with others to make simple sentences on formal greetings.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner accommodates and shows kindness to others as they work in groups.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learning greetings and introductions builds on the same concept as covered in English.
